description: verbatim disk prefix is stripped, then folded
verbatim UNC prefix is stripped to a plain UNC form, then folded
the UNC literal in a verbatim prefix matches case-insensitively
a native Windows path with a trailing backslash on a subdirectory loses it
a bare drive root keeps its trailing separator
an already-canonical bare drive root is unchanged
repeated backslashes collapse to one forward slash
repeated forward slashes collapse on an already-forward-slash Windows path
a native Windows path folds cleanly
a lowercase drive letter is still Windows-shaped
a native UNC path folds to the canonical double-forward-slash form
an already-canonical UNC path is unchanged
extra internal slashes in a UNC path collapse, and the leading double slash is preserved (not folded to one)
a UNC share root with a trailing slash strips down to the bare share root
an already-canonical POSIX path is unchanged
a literal backslash in a POSIX filename is preserved, not folded, because the path is not Windows-shaped
the POSIX root is unchanged
an empty string is unchanged
a non-ASCII Windows path where the multibyte character straddles the verbatim-prefix check's byte-8 boundary (a raw byte-index slice here previously panicked; must fold cleanly instead)
a non-ASCII path with no drive letter or UNC prefix is left untouched, including its separators
a verbatim disk prefix followed immediately by non-ASCII characters strips cleanly with no boundary panic
an accented (non-ASCII, but single-byte-adjacent-safe) character folds cleanly on a Windows-shaped path
an emoji (an astral character, encoded as a UTF-16 surrogate pair in JS and 4 UTF-8 bytes in Rust) folds cleanly on a Windows-shaped path
